warnings.label: Hunstanton coast in Norfolk
warnings.message:
High tides this evening may lead to flooding. 

Flooding is possible from 17:00pm to 21:00pm on Sunday 11th October 

Locations most affected will be low lying land and roads near rivers or on the coast, with spray being seen on the seafront paths. Flood gates in the area will be closed by the Local Authority which will make access difficult. Please take notice of the Flood Sign at the top of South Beach Road. The detailed forecast is for a peak level at  King's Lynn of 3.87mAODN at 19:00pm, on 11 October, which is  0.04m above tide tables, Wind Force 2,  South Easterly. The high tide tomorrow evening at 20:00pm is expected to also be above flood alert thresholds.

We are closely monitoring the situation.
  
Avoid beaches and coastal promenades, which may be flooded. 

This message will be updated by 21:00pm on Sunday 11 October or as the situation changes.

warnings.label: Somerset coast at Porlock Weir
warnings.message:
There is no longer a threat of flooding.
Coastal conditions are expected to improve and no flooding is expected.  
We will continue to monitor the situation and will issue further alerts or warnings if necessary.  
Continue to take care on waterside roads and footpaths and don't put yourself in unnecessary danger.

warnings.label: The Essex coast from Clacton to and including, St Peters Flat and the Colne and Blackwater estuaries
warnings.description: The Essex coast from Clacton to and including, St Peters Flat and the Colne and Blackwater estuaries
warnings.message:
High tides today may lead to flooding.
Flooding is possible from 12pm to 2pm on Sunday 11th October.
Clacton Promenade, Lee-over-Sands and Brightlingsea sea front may see some wave overtopping and spray. The Strood at Mersea Island, Coast Road and car parks on the front at West Mersea, and the Hythe and Promenade at Maldon may be flooded. The detailed forecast is for a peak level at Clacton of 2.72 mAODN at 12pm, on Sunday 11th October, which is 0.15m above tide tables, Wind Force 3, Westerly. Tides will remain high over the next couple of days.
We are closely monitoring the situation .
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded.  
This message will be updated by 5:00PM on Sunday 11 October or as the situation changes.

warnings.message:
Higher than normal tides today may lead to flooding.
Flooding is possible from 12:00pm to 3:00pm on Sunday 11th October.
We expect to see high water levels around Potter Heigham, Wroxham boat yards and Ferry Road in Horning. Levels can take several hours to peak.
We are closely monitoring the situation .
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water.  
This message will be updated by 5:00PM on Sunday 11 October or as the situation changes.
